sections.title: Form and visible characters
sections.text: Tulostoma kotlabae Pouzar produces a nearly globose to slightly flattened spore sac about 10–15 mm across, chalk-white to pale grey. It is borne on a narrow white to straw-coloured stalk, often longitudinally striate and clothed in long, ragged white scales. The apical mouth (ostiole) is short-tubular, with an entire rim similar in colour to the peridium and no contrasting dark ring. At maturity, spores and capillitium form a clay-brown to rusty-brown powdery gleba.

sections.title: Peridia and habitat
sections.text: The inner peridium is thin and papery. The outer, hyphal peridium may be inconspicuous; it persists mainly around the lower sides and base of the spore sac, often retaining sand grains. The species is reported from dry, exposed calcareous sandy substrates, including grey dunes, sandy steppe and rocky grassland, among mosses and lichens. European phylogenetic studies also reveal closely related, sometimes cryptic lineages, so some specimens cannot be reliably separated by appearance alone.

sections.title: Scope and caution
sections.text: This plate illustrates general characters and cannot identify a specimen with certainty. Closely related Tulostoma species can look alike; microscopic examination of spores and capillitium, and sometimes molecular data, is needed. Edibility is not assessed here.

traits: Spore sac nearly globose to slightly flattened, white to pale grey, commonly about 10–15 mm
Stalk slender and pale, longitudinally striate, often bearing long ragged white scales
Apical ostiole short-tubular with an entire rim and no contrasting dark ring
Outer hyphal peridium often inconspicuous, remaining at the base and sometimes holding sand; mature gleba clay-brown to rusty brown
Found on dry, sandy, often calcareous ground; closely related lineages can complicate identification
safetyNote: Taxonomic and morphological reference only. Similar Tulostoma species may require microscopic or molecular confirmation. This entry and its image are not sufficient to identify a collection; edibility is not assessed.
